_about: Hand-checked, per-exchange facts for the CCXT exchange pages. Every entry cites official exchange pages (or a named practitioner source) with the date it was read. Facts that come from CCXT metadata live in ccxt_exchange_facts.json instead. Do not add region or country labels (Rob, 2026-10-23). No 'tested by us' or 'community supported' labels (Rob, 2026-10-23).

phemex.summary: Phemex is a crypto exchange founded in 2019 that offers spot trading and perpetual futures. Phemex says more than 10 million traders use it.
signup_steps: Create a Phemex account with an email address (or another sign-in method Phemex offers).
Finish identity verification (KYC) and turn on two-factor authentication.
For practice, also create a separate account on the Phemex testnet at https://testnet.phemex.com. Testnet keys only work on the testnet.
api_key_steps: Log in and open API Management from your account menu (https://phemex.com/account/api-management).
Choose Default API entry. The High Rate Limit entry is meant for heavy, professional use.
Enter a name and the IP address of the machine that will run your bot.
Pick the permission level, click Confirm and enter the email verification code.
Copy the key and secret right away. Phemex shows the key only once.
phemex.permissions: Use read and trade access. Leave withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
phemex.testnet_note: Phemex runs a full testnet at https://testnet.phemex.com with its own accounts and keys. Set ``sandbox`` to ``True`` in LumiBot to send requests there.
extra_notes: Phemex perpetual symbols use the full CCXT form, for example ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` (settled in USDT) or ``BTC/USD:BTC`` (inverse, settled in BTC). Spot is plain ``BTC/USDT``.
Phemex also offers sub-accounts, and you can share one API key with sub-accounts from API Management. A separate sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual trades.
sources: Phemex Help Center: How do I create an API key?
Phemex Help Center: share API keys with sub-accounts

bybit.summary: Bybit is a large crypto exchange for spot trading, perpetual and dated futures, and options. It has one of the most complete APIs in CCXT and is a CCXT certified exchange.
signup_steps: Create a Bybit account on the website and finish identity verification.
Wait if needed: Bybit may block API key creation for the first 48 hours after you register.
For practice, create a separate account on the Bybit testnet at https://testnet.bybit.com. Bybit also has a demo trading mode with its own keys; that is a different system from the testnet.
api_key_steps: Open API Management on the Bybit website (https://www.bybit.com/app/user/api-management). Keys cannot be made in the app.
Click Create New Key and pick System-generated API Keys.
Choose API Transaction and give the key a name.
Set the permissions (see below) and add your bot's IP address.
Enter your two-factor code, then copy the key and secret and store them safely.
bybit.permissions: Choose Read-Write. Turn on the trade permissions for what you trade: spot trading, or contract orders and positions for perpetuals. Leave withdrawals off. Freqtrade's docs list Read-Write, Contract Orders and Contract Positions for futures bots.
bybit.testnet_note: Bybit's testnet lives at https://testnet.bybit.com and its API at https://api-testnet.bybit.com. Set ``sandbox`` to ``True`` in LumiBot to use it. Bybit's demo trading mode is separate and has not been tested with LumiBot.
extra_notes: Bybit's Unified Trading Account keeps spot and derivatives in one wallet. Traders who connect bots often say to make sure it is turned on before you create keys.
CCXT has a separate exchange id, ``bybiteu``, for Bybit's EU site. It uses the api.bybit.eu API. Use the id that matches the site where you opened your account.
Run one bot per sub-account. Freqtrade warns that manual trades on the same account can confuse a bot.
sources: Bybit Help Center: How to create your API key
Bybit Learn: how to create and set up a Bybit API key
Practitioner video: automating TradingView alerts to Bybit (API key and Unified Trading steps)

bitvavo.summary: Bitvavo is a crypto exchange based in the Netherlands. It offers spot trading with prices in euros.
signup_steps: Create a Bitvavo account and finish identity verification.
Turn on two-factor authentication. Bitvavo will not let you create API keys without it.
Bitvavo has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in on the website (keys cannot be made in the app), click your name and choose Settings.
Open the API tab and click Add new API key.
Enter a name and the IP address of your bot. Separate more than one IP with commas.
Enter your two-factor code and click Confirm. Save the key and secret right away; you cannot see the secret again.
bitvavo.permissions: Turn on View access and Trade digital assets. Bitvavo needs both to read your orders and trades. Leave Withdraw digital assets off: Bitvavo warns that API withdrawals skip two-factor and email checks.
bitvavo.testnet_note: Bitvavo has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it. Always set ``sandbox`` to ``False`` in your LumiBot config. If you leave ``sandbox`` out, LumiBot turns sandbox mode on by default and CCXT fails with an error because Bitvavo has no test site.
extra_notes: Bitvavo markets are priced in euros, so use ``EUR`` as your quote asset (for example ``BTC/EUR``).
Bitvavo supports sub-accounts. An API key can be given access to sub-accounts and internal transfers, but a trading bot does not need those permissions.
sources: Bitvavo Help Center: What are API keys and how do I create them?
